messages:
anya: quick q — can we make canary rollouts auto-contain by routing to a fallback *variant* in the same region when latency/errors spike?

kevin: yeah, that's the ask we keep getting from customer SLOs. main concerns: how we detect (p99, error budget), scope (region vs global), and whether fallback is silent or surfaced to the client.

marta: +1. also need to consider capacity fallback (move to a smaller quantized variant) vs regional failover (cross-region). Both have different infra and billing implications.

sam: cost angle: if fallback spins up dedicated capacity in another region we need pre-approved budget or it will blow the reserved capacity assumptions. maybe prefer local model-variant switch first.

ryan: proposal: two-layer policy — 1) containment: switch to compatible model variant in-region if p99 > 800ms for 2m OR error_rate > 5% for 1m; 2) escalate: if containment fails or capacity low, do cross-region failover if allowed by customer.

anya: sketching config for console/API. thoughts?
```yaml
automatic_fallback:
  enabled: true
  containment:
    triggers:
      - metric: latency_p99
        op: ">"
        value: 800ms
        window: 120s
        threshold_pct: 100
      - metric: error_rate
        op: ">"
        value: 0.05
        window: 60s
    action:
      type: route_to_variant
      variant: model:open-7b-quantized
    scope: region
    cooldown: 300s
  escalation:
    allowed: true
    action: cross_region_failover
    constraints:
      cost_limit: 2000
      legal_tags: ["no-cross-border"]
```

kevin: config looks good. couple of nitpicks: 1) threshold_pct unclear — should be percent of canary traffic affected. 2) need an explicit telemetry signal for "fallback applied" so console/alerts and billing can tag requests.

marta: +1 on telemetry. we'd want a header and an event: X-Redwood-Fallback: region|variant; and a metric fallback_rate by route/model.

sam: UX question — should the fallback be reversible automatically? e.g., revert to canary when p99 back under threshold for N minutes, or require a manual confirm (button in console)?

ux-anna: from product/ux: customers want both. default = auto-recover after stable for 10m, but exposed toggle: "manual approval for rollback". need visible indicator on Rollouts page: small badge and expand to show incident window and last triggered reason.

ryan: API semantics: two options — transparent (clients see nothing except maybe header) or decorated (we return a metadata field in the response body). Transparent fav = backwards compat, but decorated fav = more clarity for upstream. we should offer both via config toggle.

anya: what about quota accounting? if we route to a cheaper quantized variant, token billing/unit price differs. need to tag all fallback requests for accurate invoicing and cost analytics.

kevin: yes. add a billing_tag in the action payload that overrides model_price_id for the duration. Also ensure dedicated-reserved customers get alerts before their reserved pool is consumed by failovers.

marta: edge case: if containment variant lacks a feature (e.g., function-calling) we must avoid silent degradation. fallback should fail open only for pure-text generation; otherwise prefer degrade with explicit client-visible notice.

sam: +1. add allow_list of compatible capabilities to the policy. if incompatible -> escalate to manual review or cross-region where capability exists.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/feature/auto-fallback-v1 to canary group C-12 (10% traffic).

anya: action items: 1) eng-runtime (ryan + kevin) to implement telemetry + header + billing tags. 2) eng-platform (marta + sam) to codify policy schema and add compatibility checks. 3) devex/ux (ux-anna) to design console affordances for toggles, badge, and incident detail. 4) add an e2e test that simulates p99 spike and validates routing and billing tags.

kevin: i'll open an RFC PR with the YAML schema and sample flows. tagging the rollout owners in the doc.

marta: can we add a small simulator in the console to preview how a policy would act on a historical trace? that would make it easier to signoff.

ux-anna: love that. will mock a UI for "simulate fallback" with trace selector.

ryan: question for legal/compliance later: cross-region failover might be disallowed by some customers; policy should default to false and require explicit opt-in.

anya: perfect. i'll summarise as PR checklist and drop into the RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:
